chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Rifah ibn Musa said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
about a man who has land (da'wah) and pays its land tax (kharaj); is there a khums due on it? He said, 'No.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.اَلضَّيْعَةُ: Land or estate, specifically agricultural land
key_terms.خَرَاجَهَا: Its land tax (kharaj), a tax on agricultural produce or land

ai.seo_question: Is khums due on agricultural land if the owner already pays the land tax (kharaj)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the fiscal relationship between land tax (*kharaj*) and the tithe (*ushr*), ruling that a landowner who pays *kharaj* is exempt from paying *ushr* on the produce. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that *kharaj* and *ushr* are generally mutually exclusive, as *kharaj* is a tax on the land itself while *ushr* is a tax on the agricultural yield, preventing double taxation for the same property. This distinction is crucial in Shia fiqh for determining the correct zakat obligations based on whether the land is conquered by force (subject to *kharaj*) or by treaty/agreement (subject to *ushr*).
